To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the open loop batch/ sequential receiver design is more robust to the signal tracking errors than the closed loop sequential receiver architecture for a number of application scenarios.

open loop batch and sequential processing approaches for GNSS signal acquisition, tracking and data bit decoding improve the tracking margin by 5-8 dB for deep GPS/INS integration scenarios, as compared to the traditional closed loop sequential processing approaches.

an open loop GNSS signal tracking design that combines batch and/or sequential processing is more robust than the traditional closed loop GNSS signal processing approach for the following important application areas: (i) GNSS/INS deep integration, (ii) GNSS/Inertial aided GNSS, and (iii) GNSS signal tracking in urban canyons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of open loop batch/ sequential processing techniques to the design of a new generation of GPS receivers.
a novel open loop batch/ sequential signal processing approach that is shown to be a promising candidate for the next generation of GNSS receivers.
the design of a GNSS receiver architecture that combines sequential and batch signal processing techniques to improve the tracking performance and robustness of the GNSS receiver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
open loop batch processing combined with closed loop sequential processing is the most efficient and optimal approach for GNSS receiver design.

open loop batch and sequential processing approaches are better suited to GNSS applications that are characterized by high dynamics, low signal to noise ratio and/or low data rate, and that require accurate and robust GNSS tracking and data bit synchronization.

the closed loop sequential processing approach is a good choice for the case of GPS/INS integration in deep integration mode, while the open loop batch/ sequential processing approach is preferable for the case of INS/GPS integration in deep integration modes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the closed loop sequential processing approach that is traditionally applied for GNSS receiver design is not the best choice for all applications.

the proposed GNSS receiver design approach that combines batch/sequential signal processing techniques and open loop tracking architecture is more robust to the GNSS signal tracking and data bit acquisition problems.
open loop batch sequential processing provides a more robust GPS tracking performance as compared to the traditional closed loop sequential receiver approach for a number of flight test scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that
open loop batch and sequential processing can be used to improve the GPS tracking margin for a number of application areas, including the case of deep integration between the GPS and the INS.
the open loop batch/ sequential receiver design is superior to the closed loop approach in terms of tracking margin and receiver performance in general.
